name: Kakadu National Park
description: Kakadu is a vast wetland-and-sandstone wilderness in Australia's Northern Territory, about 170 km southeast of Darwin. It covers nearly 20,000 square kilometres, roughly the size of Wales, from tidal flats and floodplains to rugged escarpments. Aboriginal people have lived here for tens of thousands of years, and galleries of rock art such as Ubirr's still survive. Today traditional owners help manage the park.
